k: A tuning anvil. Forty years of bells were tuned on it. There is a dent in it shaped like a word you can't quite read.
src: 'A tuning anvil. Forty years of bells were tuned on it. There is a dent in it shaped like a word you can\'t quite read.'

k: A ledger of every noon since Tolliver began. Every entry reads RANG TRUE — except seven that read FLAT — and then, today, in large shaky letters: RANG TRUE!!!
src: 'A ledger of every noon since Tolliver began. Every entry reads RANG TRUE — except seven that read FLAT — and then, today, in large shaky letters: RANG TRUE!!!'

k: A ledger of every noon since Tolliver began. Every entry reads RANG TRUE. Except the last seven, which read FLAT. FLAT. FLAT. FLAT. FLAT. FLAT. FLAT.
src: 'A ledger of every noon since Tolliver began. Every entry reads RANG TRUE. Except the last seven, which read FLAT. FLAT. FLAT. FLAT. FLAT. FLAT. FLAT.'

k: A suit of Dawnguard plate on a stand, polished to a mirror. There is a notch in the breastplate, over the heart, that has never been hammered out.
src: 'A suit of Dawnguard plate on a stand, polished to a mirror. There is a notch in the breastplate, over the heart, that has never been hammered out.'

k: A portrait: a broad, laughing knight with a ridiculous mustache, and a young woman trying very hard not to laugh with him.
src: 'A portrait: a broad, laughing knight with a ridiculous mustache, and a young woman trying very hard not to laugh with him.'

k: Mm. Warm. So warm.
src: 'Mm. Warm. So warm.'

k: They said I'd never be cold again.
src: 'They said I\'d never be cold again.'

k: Sister Mercy says if I'm good, I can go downstairs where it's warm.
src: 'Sister Mercy says if I\'m good, I can go downstairs where it\'s warm.'

k: I'm being SO good.
src: 'I\'m being SO good.'

k: The Sisters stay under watch until the Lord-Commander says otherwise.
src: 'The Sisters stay under watch until the Lord-Commander says otherwise.'

k: They keep offering me soup. I keep saying no. It's the longest conversation I've ever had.
src: 'They keep offering me soup. I keep saying no. It\'s the longest conversation I\'ve ever had.'

k: The almshouse ledger, in a neat round hand. ADMITTED: forty-one. DISCHARGED: none. Beside each name, a small mark like a closed eye.
src: 'The almshouse ledger, in a neat round hand. ADMITTED: forty-one. DISCHARGED: none. Beside each name, a small mark like a closed eye.'

k: Leek and barley soup. It smells wonderful. Under the wonderful, faintly, something sweet and sleepy.
src: 'Leek and barley soup. It smells wonderful. Under the wonderful, faintly, something sweet and sleepy.'

k: Poppy-milk. Enough to make a grown man very, very agreeable. Nobody eat the soup.
src: 'Poppy-milk. Enough to make a grown man very, very agreeable. Nobody eat the soup.'

k: Charcoal drawings on the bell tower wall: four stick-children wearing crowns. Under them, in careful letters: *THE GUTTER CORT · PIP · NELL · TUCK · WICK.* Two of the crowns have been rubbed out and drawn back in, darker.
src: 'Charcoal drawings on the bell tower wall: four stick-children wearing crowns. Under them, in careful letters: *THE GUTTER CORT · PIP · NELL · TUCK · WICK.* Two of the crowns have been rubbed out and drawn back in, darker.'

k: ...Don't look at that. That's private property. Of the Court.
src: '...Don\'t look at that. That\'s private property. Of the Court.'

k: From up here you can see the whole City of Bells: the Cathedral, the Grand Lantern, and far off to the south, the brown thread of the Pilgrim Road.
src: 'From up here you can see the whole City of Bells: the Cathedral, the Grand Lantern, and far off to the south, the brown thread of the Pilgrim Road.'

k: No time — he's getting away!
src: 'No time — he\'s getting away!'

k: The bells will ring at noon! And at noon tomorrow! And the noon after that!
src: 'The bells will ring at noon! And at noon tomorrow! And the noon after that!'

k: What a summer, eh? Feels like it'll never end.
src: 'What a summer, eh? Feels like it\'ll never end.'

k: Lysa! Your brother's looking for you. He's _always_ looking for you.
src: 'Lysa! Your brother\'s looking for you. He\'s _always_ looking for you.'

k: Hush — the Keeper's going up. Watch the gallery. It's the best part.
src: 'Hush — the Keeper\'s going up. Watch the gallery. It\'s the best part.'

k: Valve
src: 'Valve'

k: Examine
src: 'Examine'

k: The brickwork here bulges outward, cracked and sweating. There is a hollow sound behind it.
src: 'The brickwork here bulges outward, cracked and sweating. There is a hollow sound behind it.'

k: Bram. Would you?
src: 'Bram. Would you?'

k: With _pleasure._
src: 'With _pleasure._'

k: I have been wanting to hit something that didn't hit back for _days._
src: 'I have been wanting to hit something that didn\'t hit back for _days._'

k: Scratched into the brick in chalk, at about the height of an eleven-year-old: PIP WAS ERE.
src: 'Scratched into the brick in chalk, at about the height of an eleven-year-old: PIP WAS ERE.'

k: ...That's from last year. I was _exploring._
src: '...That\'s from last year. I was _exploring._'

k: A child's shoe, much too small for anyone who should be down here. The laces are still tied — in a double knot.
src: 'A child\'s shoe, much too small for anyone who should be down here. The laces are still tied — in a double knot.'

k: That's Wick's. He does double knots because he can't do bows. I keep telling him. I keep _telling_ him.
src: 'That\'s Wick\'s. He does double knots because he can\'t do bows. I keep telling him. I keep _telling_ him.'

k: A gray hooded lantern, dropped and cracked. The Sisters of Small Mercies carry ones just like it.
src: 'A gray hooded lantern, dropped and cracked. The Sisters of Small Mercies carry ones just like it.'

k: A sheet of music, soaked through. The notes run from right to left.
src: 'A sheet of music, soaked through. The notes run from right to left.'

k: Sable reads it, and hums. The hum makes your back teeth ache.
src: 'Sable reads it, and hums. The hum makes your back teeth ache.'

k: It is the Dawnsong. Backwards.
src: 'It is the Dawnsong. Backwards.'

k: Memorial
src: 'Memorial'

k: The names are worn almost smooth. Under every one, the same date: THE LONG NIGHT.
src: 'The names are worn almost smooth. Under every one, the same date: THE LONG NIGHT.'

k: A family tomb: a mother, a father, and four small names in a row. Someone has left a wooden toy horse on it. It is very old.
src: 'A family tomb: a mother, a father, and four small names in a row. Someone has left a wooden toy horse on it. It is very old.'

k: Tucked under a guttered candle on the last tomb: a loose, water-stained page.
src: 'Tucked under a guttered candle on the last tomb: a loose, water-stained page.'

k: "...the Keeper, Aldric Lorne, was in the lamp-room when the light failed. He might have gone down to the square, where his daughter {dim|████} was. He chose the Lantern. The city lived."
src: '"...the Keeper, Aldric Lorne, was in the lamp-room when the light failed. He might have gone down to the square, where his daughter {dim|████} was. He chose the Lantern. The city lived."'

k: The great bell of the old foundry, cracked from crown to lip. Whatever was ringing it wanted very badly to be heard.
src: 'The great bell of the old foundry, cracked from crown to lip. Whatever was ringing it wanted very badly to be heard.'

k: Ring
src: 'Ring'

k: Bars
src: 'Bars'

k: A woman curled on a cot, humming. When you say hello, she says it back — in exactly your voice.
src: 'A woman curled on a cot, humming. When you say hello, she says it back — in exactly your voice.'

k: An old man counting on his fingers. He gets to nine and starts again. He has been doing it, he says, for a very long time. Or possibly since this morning.
src: 'An old man counting on his fingers. He gets to nine and starts again. He has been doing it, he says, for a very long time. Or possibly since this morning.'

k: This cell is empty, except for a pair of boots standing neatly side by side. The boots are still warm.
src: 'This cell is empty, except for a pair of boots standing neatly side by side. The boots are still warm.'

k: Mercy's notes, in a neat round hand:
src: 'Mercy\'s notes, in a neat round hand:'

k: _Subject 31: no resistance. Children rarely resist — their memories are short and sweet. The body accepts the Gloam if it is given a memory to hold. Without one, the Gloam makes only beasts._
src: '_Subject 31: no resistance. Children rarely resist — their memories are short and sweet. The body accepts the Gloam if it is given a memory to hold. Without one, the Gloam makes only beasts._'

k: _Day 40. Another beast. What did HE do differently? What did he give her to hold?_
src: '_Day 40. Another beast. What did HE do differently? What did he give her to hold?_'

k: "He." Who's "he"?
src: '"He." Who\'s "he"?'

k: Her boss, maybe. Everyone's got a boss.
src: 'Her boss, maybe. Everyone\'s got a boss.'

k: Sable says nothing at all.
src: 'Sable says nothing at all.'

k: A cot with leather straps. The straps are child-sized.
src: 'A cot with leather straps. The straps are child-sized.'

k: Pressed inside one of Mercy's ledgers, a page from an old chronicle, annotated in red ink.
src: 'Pressed inside one of Mercy\'s ledgers, a page from an old chronicle, annotated in red ink.'

k: In the margin, in fresh red ink: _Not lost. Only waiting._
src: 'In the margin, in fresh red ink: _Not lost. Only waiting._'

k: The crucible. At the bottom, a residue like burnt sugar, and a smell like a summer afternoon.
src: 'The crucible. At the bottom, a residue like burnt sugar, and a smell like a summer afternoon.'

k: THE PILGRIM ROAD — east to Saltglass.nCarry water. Carry more water than that.
src: 'THE PILGRIM ROAD — east to Saltglass.\nCarry water. Carry more water than that.'

k: Walking to Saltglass to hear the blind Keeper. They say she can name your Crest before the Lantern does.
src: 'Walking to Saltglass to hear the blind Keeper. They say she can name your Crest before the Lantern does.'

k: They say she told the Hierophant something once that made him leave in the middle of the night.
src: 'They say she told the Hierophant something once that made him leave in the middle of the night.'

k: I'd like to know what. I'd like to know anything, really. That's why I walk.
src: 'I\'d like to know what. I\'d like to know anything, really. That\'s why I walk.'

k: Ysmay's water is the last sweet water for thirty leagues. After that it's the oasis, or the town, or you drink sand.
src: 'Ysmay\'s water is the last sweet water for thirty leagues. After that it\'s the oasis, or the town, or you drink sand.'

k: Mind the glass flats. Folk see things out there. Then they walk toward them.
src: 'Mind the glass flats. Folk see things out there. Then they walk toward them.'

k: A Choir milestone: AURENNE — 40 LEAGUES. SALTGLASS — 30.
src: 'A Choir milestone: AURENNE — 40 LEAGUES. SALTGLASS — 30.'

k: Below, older letters someone tried to chisel away: "...WHERE THE LIGHT GOES, WE GO."
src: 'Below, older letters someone tried to chisel away: "...WHERE THE LIGHT GOES, WE GO."'

k: Pilgrim's Arch
src: 'Pilgrim\'s Arch'

k: A pilgrims' cairn. Every stone has a name scratched on it. Some of the names are very small, like children wrote them.
src: 'A pilgrims\' cairn. Every stone has a name scratched on it. Some of the names are very small, like children wrote them.'

k: Sarn says we're not thieves. We're a toll road with knives.
src: 'Sarn says we\'re not thieves. We\'re a toll road with knives.'

k: Skull
src: 'Skull'

k: The ribs of a giant wyrm arch out of the sand like the frame of a ship nobody finished building.
src: 'The ribs of a giant wyrm arch out of the sand like the frame of a ship nobody finished building.'
